title: Claude Certified Architect Foundations Practice Bank
disclaimer: Original practice questions grounded in the published blueprint and documentation. Not sourced from the live exam bank.

questions.scenario: A claims service must return a JSON object with an enum action, a numeric confidence score, and a nullable escalation_reason. Downstream automation rejects any response that does not match the schema, and retrying malformed output is not permitted.
questions.question: Which implementation most directly satisfies the requirement?

A.text: Describe the JSON format in the system prompt, include two examples, and set temperature to zero.
A.rationale: Examples and low temperature may improve consistency, but they do not guarantee schema conformance.

B.text: Set output_config.format to the required JSON Schema and validate the returned object before the automation uses it.
B.rationale: Structured outputs constrain the final response to the supplied schema, and application validation preserves the downstream trust boundary.

C.text: Define a strict tool whose input has the same schema, even though the workflow never needs to call a tool.
C.rationale: Strict tool use governs tool arguments; it is not the correct mechanism for constraining a final response when no tool call is needed.

D.text: Ask Claude to place the JSON in a fenced code block and parse the block with a repair library.
D.rationale: Repairing malformed output is probabilistic and violates the scenario's no-retry requirement.

grading.principle: Use a constrained mechanism when a scenario demands a guarantee; prompting is not a schema contract.
grading.hinge: The requirement says malformed output cannot be retried.
